items.title: Andrew Garfield’s The Uprising Sends Mixed Signals on Robin Hood Connection
items.description: Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Focus Features’ The Uprising stars Andrew Garfield in a 1381 Peasants' Revolt drama—but new marketing suggests it might actually be a stealth Robin Hood origin story.

“To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero. Witness the rise of Robin Hood in The Uprising, only in theaters September 11,” according to this post from the film’s official X account. Until this point in the publicity campaign, none of the movie’s marketing materials revealed any such ties to the iconic outlaw.

This ad revealed the film’s new title as The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood. It shows Garfield’s character, dressed in a green hood, emerging from the woods to confront the King and his soldiers. He is accompanied by his fellow highwaymen, who wield bows and arrows. “There will be no peace until we are free. Time to pay,” Garfield’s character declares at swordpoint.

To the rich, he was an outlaw. To the people, he was a hero. Witness the rise of Robin Hood in THE UPRISING, only in theaters September 11.

— The Uprising (@theuprisingmov) August 20, 2026

A day after this ad was released the film’s title was changed back to being just The Uprising.

The film’s UK distributor even released a statement denying The Uprising is a Robin Hood movie (via Metro): “Marketing materials posted by other countries that may appear in the UK online and on social media referencing Robin Hood are not issued or approved by us.”

The Uprising had been understood to be about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, which was led by historical figures Wat Tyler (played by Shogun’s Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (played by Jamie Bell). Garfield’s character Ploughman was thought to represent the Everyman peasant pushed by misfortune into taking up arms against the crown.

The Uprising’s original US production notes – made available in advance to stateside press for the film’s junket – did not reveal any ties to Robin Hood. Garfield’s character was referred to as merely Ploughman. The original plot synopsis read:

“Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.”

But the latest production notes, released to US press late last week, contained this updated synopsis: “Andrew Garfield stars as the leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. Set against the true events of the Uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice.”

These same updated US production notes later state: “The 14th century English poem ‘Piers Plowman’ — a simple farmer’s dream about his hopes and fears — was the inspiration for the character of the Ploughman and helped the filmmaker [Paul Greengrass] settle on his approach. (Notably, the same poem gave birth to the legend of ‘Robin Hoode,’ the ultimate British outlaw myth about a common man attempting to right great injustice and coming under threat from the authorities for his actions to serve the citizenry.)”

With The Uprising just a few short weeks away from theatrical release, any such conflicting messaging about what the film’s about risks confusing or turning off potential audiences.

If The Uprising is indeed a Robin Hood film then it will arrive on the heels of the Hugh Jackman-starring The Death of Robin Hood, a box office bomb that grossed less than $7 million worldwide against a reported production budget of $20 million.

items.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Opens Up on Future of Physical Games for Next Generation Console Project Helix
items.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.

Speaking with the BBC in August 2026, Sharma didn’t give a straight answer; instead, she said Xbox is currently focused on making its next generation hardware cost-effective and efficient.

“This next generation, we have to be thinking about efficiency and affordability alongside performance," she told the outlet.

"All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency," she continued. "That is something that we have not had to do. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."

While she couldn’t outright confirm or deny the existence of a disc drive for Project Helix, Sharma is well-aware of the current debate surrounding physical media, and assured the BBC that she wants to give players a choice when it comes to how they choose to purchase content.

"I know players love physical media, and I know there's a lot of benefits in digital media, and I want to make sure people have a choice. There are stacks of games on everybody's shelves,” she said.

Although it wasn’t exactly a clear answer, her statement does give a positive impression of Xbox’s future plans for physical games — something the brand is already winning points for, having recently confirmed an initiative that will allow players to digitize their physical games into an online library.

First leaked earlier this summer, Xbox officially announced its disc-to-digital program on August 26 during Gamescom, which will roll out for Xbox Insiders starting on August 31 before becoming available to all players at an as-yet unconfirmed date.

This makes Xbox — which recently underwent one of the most significant restructurings in the company’s history — look pretty good in comparison to PlayStation, whose decision to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028 has unsurprisingly turned out to be quite unpopular.

Disgruntled gamers are taking to the comments section of every social media post from the company to spread awareness about the ordeal, but Sony isn’t alone — GTA 6, the most highly-anticipated game in recent memory, is also forgoing a physical disc in favor of a digital code inside a disc case. Developer Rockstar has stood firm in its decision to bypass an actual disc, with Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick saying discs “don’t really make sense for the consumer.”

For now, it's anyone's guess as to what Project Helix will end up looking like when it comes to physical game discs, but previous reporting has hinted that it will likely be fully digital.

items.title: Double Fine Productions Makes Brutal Legend Free for 666 Minutes to Honor Tim Curry
items.description: Double Fine Productions, who recently regained the rights to its entire catalog following its pivot back to independence after Microsoft parted ways with several studios during its "Xbox reset," is honoring Tim Curry by making Brutal Legend free to download and own on PC for 666 minutes – until 3:06am PT/6:06am ET on Thursday, August 27.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Double Fine Productions, who recently regained the rights to its entire catalog following its pivot back to independence after Microsoft parted ways with several studios during its "Xbox reset," is honoring Tim Curry by making Brutal Legend free to download and own on PC for 666 minutes – until 3:06am PT/6:06am ET on Thursday, August 27.

Curry, who passed away today at the age of 80, voiced Doviculus in Double Fine founder Tim Schafer's 2009 heavy metal strategy game Brutal Legend. "Rest in peace, dark prince," the company wrote on its itch.io page where you can download the game on PC. IGN's own Daemon Hatfield loved Brutal Legend, giving it a 9 out of 10 in his review. "Brutal Legend is a tour de force that wraps up humor, music, and clever gameplay into one highly polished package," Daemon wrote. "You haven't played a game quite like this before and won't want to miss it."

Curry was perhaps best known for his role in the cult classic film The Rocky Horror Picture Show, but also appeared in many video games besides Brutal Legend, including Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 (back in the FMV cutscene days!), Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers, and Dragon Age: Origins.

Double Fine, meanwhile, has announced that it is using its newfound independence to bring back its Amnesia Fortnight game jam as it looks to create its next project(s).

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Silent Hill Producer Says Konami Wants to Release a New Game in the Series Every Year
items.description: Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says that Konami is gunning for annual releases of new games in its flagship horror franchise.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says that Konami is gunning for annual releases of new games in its flagship horror franchise.

Okamoto divulged this news in an interview with Gamesradar at Gamescom 2026, explaining that Konami is looking for fresh takes on the well-trodden beats of the Silent Hill series to keep it from stagnating.

"Our aim is to, hopefully, have an annual release of new games," he told the outlet. “If we stay laser-focused on the same American setting, that would exhaust [narrative] possibilities, and also potentially cause fatigue for the playerbase."

Okamoto also confirmed that several unannounced Silent Hill projects are currently in development. "There are still many projects that are still [in] the works and very unannounced titles. So obviously, we can't go into specifics. But there are still many projects that we are currently exploring and working on as we speak,” he said.

"We would like to let players know that we have more experiences coming up, and many types of games that, we believe, will be able to provide positive kinds of surprises for players waiting for this for the series."

This information holds up with statements made by Konami’s president, Hideki Hayakawa, who said the company is actively invested in “rebooting” its most iconic IPs, specifically mentioning Silent Hill, Metal Gear, and Castlevania. (Though, in this case, the word 'reboot' seems to mean reinvigorating the franchises with new games, rather than remaking old ones.)

“Our company has been making games for more than 50 years, and we hold several IPs that are beloved globally by many fans. We concluded that rebooting these properties would be an effective way to make the most of them,” he said in an interview with Nikkei Gaming on July 23. “In addition to Metal Gear, Silent Hill, and Momotaro Dentetsu, we are also actively developing Castlevania (known in Japan as Akumajō Dracula).

“Our basic philosophy is that as long as there are customers for a given game, we will release it across multiple devices. Rather than focusing intensely on just one specific IP, we’ve built a structure that allows us to push forward on multiple IPs simultaneously with equal energy. That’s what this past year has looked like for us,” he explained.

Silent Hill has enjoyed a second wind with the Silent Hill 2 Remake and Silent Hill f, alongside the upcoming Silent Hill: Townfall, set to release on September 22. Silent Hill f, specifically, seems in line with Konami’s goals for the series, taking a drastic shift from its usual American setting in favor of 1960s Japan.

For more Silent Hill news, check out the official cast reveal trailer for Silent Hill Townfall and keep an eye out on our coverage from this year’s Gamescom.

Honorable Mention: Silent Hill 2

There were doubts as to whether Bloober Team could faithfully remake one of the most beloved horror games of all time. Even Bloober admitted as much, citing the mixed reception some of their previous horror games have received. But the determination to do right by the source material paid off as Silent Hill 2 delivers one of the scariest – and best – gaming experiences of the year. Faithful to everything that made the original great, while updating the rusty, aging bits beautifully, Silent Hill 2 embodies everything that’s great about the original and then some.

items.title: 'I Think That Was a Big Flaw' — Uncharted 3 Designer Says the Game Was Hindered by Too Many Set Pieces
items.description: An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted 3 was developed.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
An ex-Naughty Dog designer believes that Uncharted 2's success may have negatively impacted the way Uncharted 3 was developed.

When speaking with FRVR, ex-Naughty Dog designer Benson Russell revealed that Uncharted 2's over-the-top setpieces may have negatively impacted Uncharted 3. He noted that the big set pieces, such as the train sequence, all came organically when producing the game, but that wasn't the case for Uncharted 3. Instead, the team came up with 10 or 12 set pieces, such as the cargo plane sequence, and came up with a plan to decide on a small handful that would actually make it into the game at a later date.

Unfortunately, that never happened, and almost all of them made it into the final product. As a result, writer and director Amy Hennig was forced into a situation where she had to write all of these big set pieces into the game because the designers had already started working on them.

“It also kind of corners Amy [Hennig] a bit, right?” he said. “Because it’s like, ‘Oh, these are the set pieces we want to do’, and she’s like, ‘Well, now I have to find a way to shoehorn the ship in, so I guess we’ll have pirates and they’ll have a pirate leader.'"

Russell went on to say that he believes making the game in this way was "a big flaw." Uncharted 3 sold exceptionally well and was highly reviewed, even scoring a 10/10 from IGN at the time. However, it does rank lower on the list when compared to other games in the series. The cargo plane sequence, however, is a standout moment that even made its way into the Uncharted live-action film a decade later.

Naughty Dog concluded the Uncharted series back in 2016, but there are rumors that the studio is returning for Uncharted 5 soon. Although its only announced title is Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, Naughty Dog has confirmed that it has multiple projects in the works. As for when we'll start to see those other games, it's hard to say, but it wouldn't be surprising if they follow Intergalatic in a relatively rapid succession.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Chris Hansen Buys Advertisements for His True Crime Streaming Platform Before Every Single Screening of A24's Primetime Movie
items.description: Chris Hansen, best known as the host of Dateline NBC’s To Catch a Predator series, has purchased advertisements for his streaming platform that will play before every single screening of A24’s upcoming film adaptation of his rise to fame, Primetime.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Chris Hansen, best known as the host of Dateline NBC’s To Catch a Predator series, has purchased advertisements for his streaming platform that will play before every single screening of A24’s upcoming film adaptation of his rise to fame, Primetime.

The Hollywood Reporter received exclusive footage of the trailer, which reportedly shows the host walking into a kitchen before greeting viewers with a familiar line: “I’m going to need everyone in the theater to take a seat right over there.”

“Now, there are more platforms than ever before where this disturbing crime is being committed. Join us undercover every day on my streaming network, TruBlu,” he says as a QR code pops up on the screen.

TruBlu is a true crime-focused streaming network co-founded and co-owned by Hansen, which features undercover stings, investigative reporting, crime documentaries, and other such fare. According to The Hollywood Reporter, Hansen’s original plan for his TruBlu advertisement included a line calling A24’s Primetime movie a “Hollywood fantasy version” of real events — but due to fears of backlash from arthouse studio, it was cut from the final version.

It’s safe to say that Hansen isn’t too keen on Primetime. The host notably turned down a preliminary screening of the film, as told by the man himself during an interview with Fox News where he accused A24 of asking him to sign a “very restrictive agreement” before he could sit down in the theater.

“The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image, and brand, essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie,” he stated. “I couldn’t sign that, so they didn’t show me the film. I went all the way over there. … But who’s going to sign something like that?

“If you look at the trailer, obviously it’s a very dramatized version. They had told me that it’s fictionalized in many aspects. I know other people have seen it who didn’t sign an NDA, and yet they wanted me to sign it.”

This claim was refuted by sources close to the situation, who told The Hollywood Reporter that Hansen was merely asked to sign a standard NDA to “prevent spoilers and protect the studio’s IP.”

Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, was partially inspired by a 2007 Esquire article penned by Luke Dittrich that focused on Texas District Attorney Bill Conradt, who committed suicide after becoming the target of one of Hansen’s predator stings. Primetime releases in theaters on September 25, 2026.

It’s safe to say that Hansen isn’t too keen on Primetime. The host notably turned down a preliminary screening of the film, as told by the man himself during an interview with Fox News where he accused A24 of asking him to sign a “very restrictive agreement” before he could sit down in the theater.

“The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image, and brand, essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie,” he stated. “I couldn’t sign that, so they didn’t show me the film. I went all the way over there. … But who’s going to sign something like that?

“If you look at the trailer, obviously it’s a very dramatized version. They had told me that it’s fictionalized in many aspects. I know other people have seen it who didn’t sign an NDA, and yet they wanted me to sign it.”

This claim was refuted by sources close to the situation, who told The Hollywood Reporter that Hansen was merely asked to sign a standard NDA to “prevent spoilers and protect the studio’s IP.”

Primetime, starring Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, was partially inspired by a 2007 Esquire article penned by Luke Dittrich that focused on Texas District Attorney Bill Conradt, who committed suicide after becoming the target of one of Hansen’s predator stings. Primetime releases in theaters on September 25, 2026.

items.title: Ridley Scott Is Developing an Alien: Covenant Sequel With Michael Fassbender
items.description: Ridley Scott has confirmed he isn't done with the Alien franchise as he's developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Ridley Scott has confirmed he isn't done with the Alien franchise, as he's developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant.

When speaking with the LA Times, Scott confirmed he is still developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant, one that would follow Michael Fassbender's character, David. Scott revealed that the film would see David creating a “brave new world for himself" and deal with AI going awry. The android character was introduced in Scott's Alien prequel, Prometheus, and returned for Alien: Covenant. Throughout the two films, it has become extremely clear that his character plays a significant role in the Alien universe.

The end of Covenant teased that his story was far from over, but that follow-up film has been in development hell for nearly a decade. Covenant itself missed the mark financially, and then Fox was acquired by Disney, which likely caused all kinds of issues with the film's development. Still, the Alien IP is very active with FX's Alien: Earth series and 2024's Alien: Romulus, which was a big hit. There's also the highly-anticipated Alien: Isolation 2 on the horizon for gamers.

Ridley Scott had previously stated that he wanted to make a whole series of Alien prequels that lead into the original film, and his follow-up to Covenant would be one of many entries to build up to that. As of right now, it's unclear when Ridley Scott plans to break out the chestbursters again. He just released The Dog Stars, starring Jacob Elordi (which IGN gave a 5), and has a Treasure Planet adaptation with Hugh Jackman set to begin filming in November, a Bee Gees project at Paramount, and a variety of original films in different stages of development.

Scott is a prolific director who cranks out a movie every other year at this point, but he's also 88. He doesn't have any plans to stop making movies, but it'll be interesting to see if he can get to the next Alien movie within the next couple of years. A sequel to Alien: Romulus is also in the works at Fox, but there's no word on when that will arrive either.

items.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Will Include Two Sneak Peeks at Doomsday, But There's a Catch
items.description: Two sneak peeks at Avengers: Doomsday are coming to screenings of Avengers: Endgame Encore, though one of them will only be included in certain showings.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Two sneak peeks at Avengers: Doomsday are coming to screenings of Avengers: Endgame Encore, though one of them will only be included in certain showings.

As per an August 25 press release from Disney UK, Avengers: Endgame Encore will include an “exclusive look” at Avengers: Doomsday. It’s expected that this will at least partially account for the four extra minutes that have been added to the film’s total runtime, which fans noticed when AMC began listing showtimes late last week.

In bigger news, an “additional sneak peek” of the upcoming flick will also be included at showings on IMAX and Infinity Vision-certified screens. Thus far, it’s unclear how much time this will add to those screenings, and it’s possible that this glimpse at Doomsday could be part of the pre-show previews and not the actual film itself. Either way, fans are split as to whether or not sitting through a three hour-long movie they’ve already seen is actually worth it.

Avengers director Joe Russo has said it’s “critically important” that Marvel Studios re-release the film in theaters, calling it an "opportunity to create a bridge from Endgame to Doomsday in a very unique way.”

"You don’t always get the chance to re-release because it costs money, so the fact that we can enhance the story of Doomsday by bridging it to Endgame and these characters that we worked with for years that we love so much, and continue their story: It’s a really unique opportunity,” he said.

As told by Russo, Avengers Endgame: Encore will contain “footage that is set in the Doomsday story” that has been added to Endgame. It’s unclear as yet what this footage will be, exactly, but launching DLC for a seven-year-old film is rubbing some Marvel fans the wrong way.

According to one fan on Reddit, "It's literally four extra minutes of footage that will be in a YouTube short within two days," while another argued that it’s not worth the trouble of “getting a babysitter” and “spending $30-$40 for four minutes of footage.”

Avengers: Doomsday is shaping up to be a similarly-debated film; Robert Downey Jr.’s role as Victor Von Doom has left some fans convinced that Marvel is holding an ace up its sleeve, with theories abounding that, perhaps, the actor so iconic for playing Iron Man is merely an illusion or a different version of the character in an alternate reality.

Still others have noticed apparent changes in Dr. Doom’s eye color in different shots within Doomsday trailers, suggesting that these theories could hold some merit. For now, Marvel has been playing its cards close to the chest as the Doomsday clock ticks down to December 18, 2026.

items.title: Doom Composer Mick Gordon Contributes New Track to Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2
items.description: Auroch Digital and Big Fan Games have confirmed award-winning composer Mick Gordon has contributed a new track to its upcoming ’90s-inspired boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Auroch Digital and Big Fan Games have confirmed award-winning composer Mick Gordon has contributed a new track to its upcoming ’90s-inspired boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2.

The first taste of the original track can be heard behind today’s new release date trailer for Boltgun 2, which is blasting its way onto PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 14. It was additionally confirmed Boltgun 2 will also be coming to Switch 2 “shortly after” its debut on other platforms.

The trailer showcases the first footage of the game’s chief antagonist, Vashtorr the Arkifane – described as the “daemonic demigod of inventors, engineers, scientists, and artisans.”

IGN’s latest preview of Boltgun 2 found it “brings the grimy, oppressive reality of the 42nd Millennium to life with a readable, pixelated style that evokes the essence of it in a way that even the most hyperrealistic renditions like Space Marine 2 struggle to match”, and that it “feels like undiluted 40K.”

Mick Gordon’s soundtracks for both 2016’s Doom and Doom Eternal are the stuff of legend, although they ultimately culminated in a very public feud involving Gordon and Doom Eternal executive producer Marty Stratton.

Despite this, however, it was announced earlier this month that Gordon will be performing the Doom 2016 soundtrack live at UK-based tech-metal and prog music festival RADAR 2027. While Gordon performed a medley of Doom tracks at The Game Awards 2016, RADAR 2027 will otherwise mark the first time the soundtrack has been performed in a live environment like this.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Yu-Gi-Oh x Crocs Collaboration Revealed Ahead of World Championship
items.description: Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Crocs and Konami have revealed a new line of clogs inspired by the Yu-Gi-Oh trading card game and anime series.

The collaboration was shown off in a display case ahead of this year's Yu-Gi-Oh World Championship in Tokyo. The line will seemingly include four new pairs of Crocs, two standard and two in the Echo style, each of which is themed after specific characters and cards. Those attending the World Championship also got a look at a new limited-edition Yu-Gi-Oh card themed after the collection.

The Crocs website has a section dedicated to the collaboration, but individual listings have yet to appear. Konami and Crocs have yet to confirm a wide release date or pricing, but some outlets are reporting a potential release in September.

OFFICIAL LOOK: Yu-Gi-Oh! x Crocs Collection 🃏🐉

Classic Clogs
- Yugi Yami
- Seto Kaiba

Echo Clogs
- Dark Magician
- Blue-Eyes White Dragon

🗓️ September 2026 pic.twitter.com/iB9HWKqofE

— Sole Retriever (@SoleRetriever) August 25, 2026

The four Crocs shown off at the World Championship can be seen above. The two standard Clogs are themed after Yugi Mutou, the show’s main character, and his rival Seto Kaiba. The colorways are largely inspired by their respective outfits, Decks, and, of course, Yugi’s iconic hair.

The Echo clogs have quite a bit more dimension, and are both themed after specific cards that also make appearances in the original anime. One pair takes its purple inspiration from the Dark Magician. The other is inspired by none other than the legendary Blue-Eyes White Dragon, Seto’s go-to creature and one of the most valuable cards in real life.

Promotional images also suggest the collaboration will feature a line of Jibbitz, including accessories modeled after straight-up Yu-Gi-Oh cards.

Yu-Gi-Oh really committed to the Crocs collab 😭🐊

Alongside four character-inspired Crocs, they made a “Crocodile” promo card featuring an actual crocodile WEARING Crocs 😂

It’s even Level 3 with 1300 ATK/DEF and flavor text referencing the 13 holes on its feet. pic.twitter.com/49qErCc2Tm

— The Collectibles Guru (@gurucollects) August 25, 2026

Speaking of cards, the Crocs-themed card that was shown off at the convention is simply titled ‘Crocodile,’ a Reptile/Normal card with 1300 ATK and 1300 DEF. Fun fact: Crocs have exactly 13 holes in them. Images posted online don’t appear to show any special card effects, but it could be an interesting grab for collectors.

At this point, there’s no word on whether the card will be available for purchase or included as part of the Crocs collection.

Crocs has truly been going full LEGO mode with the collaborations, including Animal Crossing, Super Mario, and over the next couple of months, Pokemon-themed clogs. They’re not the only shoes looking to franchises, either - a Pokemon x Adidas collaboration is dropping in early September, while Nike just revealed a new One Piece collection.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: Rockstar Games Doubled in Size for GTA 6, Hired Real World Professionals for Fashion, Vehicles, and More
items.description: Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games doubled its employee headcount for Grand Theft Auto 6 and hired real-world professionals for the game's vehicles, fashion, and more.

As part of a cover story for Dazed, Rockstar Games shared a boatload of information about Grand Theft Auto 6. In the piece, it was confirmed that Rockstar doubled in size following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2 in order to bring GTA 6 to life, with a new Los Angeles-based office being "almost solely" dedicated to working on nothing but the game's NPCs. For context, Rockstar had around 2,000 employees in 2018. That would put them at around 4,000 now. The studio has expanded a lot over the last decade by acquiring new studios in Australia, India, and the aforementioned LA office.

Rockstar's expansion doesn't exclusively encompass game developers. The company brought on other real-world professionals, such as Miami-based stylist Jillian Carr, who was hired to help create a “fashion ecosystem” that can capture the diversity in style, culture, and class necessary to give Vice City's people their distinct character.

“Vice City is built around vanity,” Carr said to the magazine. “Between social media, celebrity culture and a constant flow of tourists, appearances carry significant weight, and trend cycles turn over quickly.”

Rockstar also hired racecar drivers to help with vehicle handling and 50 real street artists to design murals around the game's map. While consultants are hardly unique to this project, Carr and others are full-time employees at Rockstar and have been for years. Carr was specifically hired in 2023 and appears to be as much of the team's regular operations as anyone else.

Rockstar also revealed new gameplay details for GTA 6, such as how eating, working out, and sleeping all impact your characters and much, much more. It's just the start of a larger bombardment of GTA 6 information, too. Rockstar will officially pull the veil off the game tomorrow in an extended look on Netflix, which is widely expected to give us a deep dive on gameplay.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Gets Pending Mature 17+ Rating, and Fan Theories Are Already Going Wild
items.description: Final Fantasy VII Revelation is available to wishlist on all major platforms, and fans have noticed that its pending rating is a bit more intense than they expected.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Final Fantasy VII Revelation is available to wishlist on all major platforms, and fans have noticed that its pending rating on the Xbox store is a bit more intense than they expected.

Set to release in Spring 2027, the last entry in the Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy wraps up the saga for Cloud and company in their quest to protect the planet from the incoming Meteor.

We’ve gotten a few glimpses at gameplay over the last few months, showing off submarine combat, traversal via the Highwind, and an explanation of the new FITS system — but none of these point to a Mature rating.

That’s the current predicted rating that’s listed on the game’s Xbox page, which says, “Rating pending, likely Mature 17+.” As clarified by the ESRB’s rating system, the Mature rating is given to games that may contain “intense violence, blood and gore, sexual content and/or strong language.”

For now, the game’s rating is still pending, and the Mature prediction is simply a placeholder implemented by the ESRB likely based on many publicly unknown factors prior to its official rating. But why would Revelation be rated Mature, when the first two games in the trilogy were rated T for Teen?

There’s a couple possible explanations for this. The first could be that the ESRB is using the placeholder out of an abundance of caution due to Final Fantasy XVI, which was notably rated Mature due to its sexual themes, language, and overall violence.

The other explanation is that there could be a lot more violence, language, and sexual themes in this particular game… and that possibility is sending fans into a tizzy.

Most can’t help but bring up that saucy scene between Clive and Jill in FF16, wondering if the famous "Highwind scene" between Cloud and Tifa might get a bit more heated than was originally portrayed in the 1997 game.

“I BEG YOUR FINEST PARDON?” one fan wrote on X. “Mature 17+?! Spicy Highwind scene confirmed??? Hello?!”

I BEG YOUR FINEST PARDON

Mature 17+?!

Spicy Highwind scene confirmed????
Hello?! pic.twitter.com/qVJJ4aHjMB

— ✨🌙✨ (@TifaTheMonk) August 26, 2026

“FFVII Revelation may go M rated? This would make it the second mainline game to do so, and I welcome it,” another said. “I want Final Fantasy to embrace that mature rating to explore their heavy, more darker themes with a grace and gravitas that gets muddied by having to compromise.”

FFVII Revelation may go M rated? This would make it the second mainline game to do so and I welcome it.

I want Final Fantasy to embrace that mature rating to explore their heavy, more darker themes with a grace and gravitas that gets muddied by having to compromise.

FFXVI was… pic.twitter.com/QJMuJqRsoy

— Limitless (@MoreLimitless) August 26, 2026

For now, it’s anyone’s guess as to whether or not this pending rating will actually stick. In the meantime, you can check out the most recent reveals for the game, which were shown off at Gamescom’s Opening Night Live showcase along with several other significant gaming announcements.

items.title: Apple iPhone Event Invites Have Gone Out, and I Want a Foldable iPhone
items.description: There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those is that Apple is going to host a big, flashy event in September to show off its new iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those things is Apple hosting a big, flashy event in September to show off its newest iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.

The event will happen September 9 at 10am PST, and while the company hasn't shared exactly what's in store, it's not hard to guess that this is where all the latest iPhones are going to get showcased. As for which iPhones will be getting a refresh, its anyone's guess, but it's safe to assume that the iPhone 18 and its Pro version will be there, along with the latest Apple Watch.

But rumors have circled for ages that Apple has been toying with the idea of launching a foldable phone. It feels like this is something that I've been hearing for years now, but with how far foldables have come in the last two years, specifically, this could be the year that Apple finally brings its version to the masses – after all, it has named this iteration of the event "Surprise and Shine." A foldable iPhone would certainly be surprising, to say the least.

Back in July, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Quo predicted that the foldable iPhone would be coming sometime this year, but that it would be in limited supply, with "7–8 million units, with 3Q26 shipments at 0.5–1 million units, or about 10% of the total." He also predicted that if the foldable is real, it'd be quite expensive. That shouldn't be surprising, though, with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra costing $2,100 when it launched last month.

While that would mean Apple would be quite late to the foldable game, the company has a track record of taking technologies and launching them into the stratosphere. It's hard to imagine that a $2,000 phone is going to have mainstream success, but if any company could do it, it'd be Apple.

Beyond the rumored foldable, though, I don't suspect that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro are going to be that different from the iPhone 17. The 17 Pro brought a new chassis, with a much better camera shelf, and I'd expect Apple to ride that chassis out for another year.

Whichever iPhones Apple elects to launch this year will probably come with a modest price bump, though. The RAM crisis does apply to phones, and the company has already raised prices on the rest of its product lineup. It wouldn't be surprising, then, that the new iPhone is going to have at least some price increase baked in. At least that would help the company avoid raising prices on older products.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Fans Mourn Tim Curry After Legendary Actor Dies at 80 Years Old
items.description: Prolific British actor Tim Curry has died aged 80, leaving behind a storied legacy that includes iconic roles in productions like The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Muppet Treasure Island, Home Alone 2, and many more.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Prolific British actor Tim Curry has died aged 80, leaving behind a storied legacy that includes iconic roles in productions like The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Muppet Treasure Island, Home Alone 2, and many more.

News of Curry’s death was announced on August 26, 2026 by his long-term manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz, who confirmed the star died at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles.

Curry suffered a severe stroke in 2012 that left him wheelchair bound, causing lasting issues in his left leg. The actor opened up about the incident in an interview with CBS in October 2025, revealing that the stroke had even impacted his ability to speak.

“I had to learn how to speak again,” he explained. “That was very weird. I hated not being able to speak because I speak a lot. I have to be told to shut up a lot. I love words, I love to communicate.”

Despite his physical limitations as a result of the stroke, Curry continued to work, notably returning to Rocky Horror for the 2016 televised remake of the musical as the story’s narrator, The Criminologist.

Curry was born on April 19, 1946 in Grappenhall, Cheshire. He graduated from the University of Birmingham with a BA in English and drama in 1968. That same year, he joined the original cast of the musical Hair in London, a project that would lead him to meet actor and playwright Richard O’Brien, who famously penned his role as Dr Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show.

Curry’s performance in the musical, which came to film in 1975, skyrocketed the actor to fame, kicking off the heyday of his career in the 90s and 2000s. Millennials will remember him best as the cagey hotel concierge from Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, Long John Silver in Muppet Treasure Island, and Pennywise the Clown in the 1990 miniseries adaptation of Steven King’s IT.

Curry also boasted a swath of famous voice acting roles, having lent his talents to animated films like FernGully: The Last Rainforest, The Wild Thornberries Movie, and the English dub of Studio Ghibli’s The Cat Returns.

Curry’s last major role in a live-action film was playing Alexander Monro in the 2010 British comedy Burke & Hare. He notably made an appearance at a September 2025 screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show for the film’s 50th anniversary, where he shared more details about his stroke.

“I was having a massage at the time and I didn’t even actually notice anything, but the guy who was doing the massage said, ‘I’m worried about you, I want to call an ambulance.’ And he did, and I said, ‘That’s so silly.’ I still can’t walk, which is why I’m in this silly chair, and that’s very limiting. So I won’t be singing and I won’t be dancing very soon. I still have real problems with my left leg,” the actor shared.

As noted by The Hollywood Reporter, Curry answered that he wasn’t afraid of dying in response to a question during his October 2025 interview with CBS. “No, I’m not. I don’t fear death. I try to avoid it, as I think we all do, but I suspect that in the end I will welcome it,” he said.

The entertainment world is mourning the loss of two legends in just as many days, with country music legend Dolly Parton's death being announced by her nephew yesterday, August 25.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More
items.description: Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-y style this time around.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-type style this time around.

As part of a cover story for Dazed magazine, Rockstar Games revealed heaps of new information about Grand Theft Auto 6. Arguably the most notable details revolve around some of its gameplay features. In GTA 6, players will be able to eat, work out, and sleep, all of which have an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Players will have to take care of the Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple, as eating will affect their weight, working out will visibly change their build and strength, and a lack of sleep will negatively impact their features. It's unclear if a lack of sleep will impact the actual gameplay, or if they'll just look sleep-deprived, but it's a clear sign of Rockstar's attention to detail.

For many, this may remind them of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. That game featured a lot of RPG mechanics that allowed CJ to fluctuate in weight and fitness. Later games largely dropped these elements, but GTA 5 featured a stat system that allowed players to enhance their stamina and strength by doing physical activities such as running, playing sports, and riding bikes.

Additionally, there is also a social media feed for players to scroll, something fans have speculated about since the game's reveal in 2023. Character switching is also returning from GTA 5, allowing players to play as a couple or split up and operate independently. Dazed teased that the relationship between these two is a major focus of the game and that choices made by the player have "repercussions that cut much deeper" than the honor system in the Red Dead Redemption series.

“We look back at our previous games with a critical eye and see where we want to evolve based on what we didn’t do as well as we would have liked to, either because we didn’t have the time, resources or technological capabilities, or in some cases things we just didn’t do as well or consider as fully as we could have,” said Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. “A lot of what we do is very iterative — we adjust a lot of things by feel based on what is working and what isn’t.”

Based on that information, it's possible that there will be some kind of relationship meter that can impact how Jason and Lucia feel about each other. Ultimately, it sounds like Rockstar is making a much more nuanced and interactive game. That should hardly come as a surprise following Red Dead Redemption 2, but it seems like Rockstar is really pushing the envelope with GTA 6. Tomorrow, fans will get a proper look at the game thanks to an extended look releasing on Netflix at 3 PM ET, with a YouTube version to follow six hours later.

GTA 6 has suffered from a plethora of leaks over the last week, including a story-focused one earlier today. Rockstar Games released a statement this morning confirming that the situation was "heartbreaking," but it is working hard to deliver a product that exceeds expectations.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19th for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park Announced
items.description: Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24.

The Manhattan-set live-service game will finally head into Central Park due to a distress call from inside it. Echoes promises a darker tone wrapped in fear and mystery, with neither players nor their in-game avatars sure about what's inside or what Central Park has been like since the outbreak.

Massive promises ample replayability for this DLC, including "a few twists" to give gameplay a unique feel. Speaking of gameplay, the developerse also want to lean heavier into gameplay here, rather than just new story content. Exactly how that will manifest itself remains to be seen.

IGN gave The Division 2 an 8.5 out of 10 back in 2019 and the 2020 DLC Warlords of New York an 8 out of 10.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Beta Will Be Playable on Switch 2 for Free This Weekend
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.

Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free. The beta's second weekend will kick off, giving Nintendo fans the opportunity to try a level from the game's campaign, multiplayer, and even the battle royale, Warzone.

The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game.

It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.

"For the first time in more than a decade, Call of Duty is back on a Nintendo platform, and we’re incredibly proud that Digital Legends has partnered with Infinity Ward to make it happen with Modern Warfare 4, said Xavier Carrillo-Costa, studio head, Digital Legends. "Our goal has been simple from day one: deliver the genuine Call of Duty experience on Nintendo Switch 2. Players can enjoy the full intensity, authenticity, and quality of Modern Warfare 4 wherever they are, whether at home or on the move."

In 2023, Microsoft signed a legally binding deal with Nintendo to bring Call of Duty games to Nintendo platforms for a decade with full feature parity. That means there's no missing content or notable concessions made to bring Call of Duty to Switch 2. Whether Nintendo fans show up for this release remains to be seen, but it's great to see Switch 2 being supported more and more by the biggest third-party franchises out there.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Leaker Posts Extended Gameplay From GTA 6 Prologue Just Hours After Rockstar Warns Fans to Expect Story Spoilers
items.description: Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks.

More than four minutes of gameplay featuring GTA 6 character Lucia is now being spread over social media, in the first lengthy leak of footage that reveals key story details. If you are planning to try and experience GTA 6 with no narrative spoilers, now is the time to beware where you click online over the coming days and weeks.

The footage's release comes just hours after Rockstar finally broke its silence over the leaks, which it called "heartbreaking" for its development team. In its statement, published online earlier today, the developer warned fans that spoilers would likely impact the manner in which it had hoped players would first experience the game — something that now appears to accurate.

A fresh statement from the leaker, included as a watermark in this latest footage, makes several unsubtantiated claims about GTA 6's development, such as the game still being unfinished and that "too much" work remains on the game to be comfortably completed before the title's November 19 release date.

Earlier today, Rockstar noted that it was indeed still working on the game — something that is fully to be expected with nearly three months left to go until launch — but that it was now "nearly" finished. The company also reiterated GTA 6's November 19 launch date, suggesting confidence that nothing would change.

The leaker has also claimed to have a "recent" build of the game, something that is again impossible to verify. However, there is now little doubt that these leaks stem from a polished playable build. Exactly how the leaker has gained access to it remains a mystery, but one which Rockstar and GTA publisher Take-Two are actively taking steps to ascertain.

Finally, the leaker once again called for "support" in the form of their own cryptocurrency, something that has been widely seen as a money-making exercise. Perhaps signalling that their leaking days may be winding down, the leaker suggested that "trading volume/price" of the $Cyberleek currency would determine whether the posting of footage will continue.

The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, causing significant damage from a Rockstar perspective as numerous sections of GTA 6's world have now been revealed. According to Bloomberg, Rockstar has been left scrambling to discover how these leaks happened and who is behind them, as they have continued now for the past week.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, has downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say that the company has weathered worse in the past, such as the Hot Coffee scandal.

Of course, all of this is happening with just a day to go until Rockstar Games' own unveiling of GTA 6 gameplay, via its Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look. This lengthy and official debut will be released exclusively on Netflix for six hours, before arriving on other platforms such as YouTube. Find out exactly when the GTA 6 Extended Look will be available where you are right here.

A fresh statement from the leaker, included as a watermark in this latest footage, makes several unsubtantiated claims about GTA 6's development, such as the game still being unfinished and that "too much" work remains on the game to be comfortably completed before the title's November 19 release date.

Earlier today, Rockstar noted that it was indeed still working on the game — something that is fully to be expected with nearly three months left to go until launch — but that it was now "nearly" finished. The company also reiterated GTA 6's November 19 launch date, suggesting confidence that nothing would change.

The leaker has also claimed to have a "recent" build of the game, something that is again impossible to verify. However, there is now little doubt that these leaks stem from a polished playable build. Exactly how the leaker has gained access to it remains a mystery, but one which Rockstar and GTA publisher Take-Two are actively taking steps to ascertain.

Finally, the leaker once again called for "support" in the form of their own cryptocurrency, something that has been widely seen as a money-making exercise. Perhaps signalling that their leaking days may be winding down, the leaker suggested that "trading volume/price" of the $Cyberleek currency would determine whether the posting of footage will continue.

The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, causing significant damage from a Rockstar perspective as numerous sections of GTA 6's world have now been revealed. According to Bloomberg, Rockstar has been left scrambling to discover how these leaks happened and who is behind them, as they have continued now for the past week.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, has downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say that the company has weathered worse in the past, such as the Hot Coffee scandal.

Of course, all of this is happening with just a day to go until Rockstar Games' own unveiling of GTA 6 gameplay, via its Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look. This lengthy and official debut will be released exclusively on Netflix for six hours, before arriving on other platforms such as YouTube. items.title: Xbox's 25th Anniversary Limited Edition Console Price and Release Date Revealed, Comes With Halo: Campaign Evolved
items.description: Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.

Earlier this summer, Microsoft revealed that it will be releasing a translucent green Xbox Series X console, inspired by the original Xbox console, for the company's 25th anniversary. Now, Microsoft has confirmed that the console will cost a whopping $899.99 and release on November 13. It will come with the Xbox Series X console, a matching controller, and a free copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Pre-orders will open tomorrow, August 27, at 7 AM PDT.

The controller can be purchased separately for $79.99, and it will release on October 20. If you're in the market for a brand new Xbox, this isn't a bad deal. The Xbox Series X itself costs $799.99 with a disc drive. This costs an extra $100 and includes one of Xbox's biggest games of the year. However, the next-generation of Xbox is also likely right around the corner. Microsoft confirmed earlier this year that it will detail its next console, codenamed Project Helix, later this year.

It wouldn't be surprising if the next Xbox releases in fall 2027, as Microsoft has already indicated that will be a really important window for the company. The company also unveiled plans for a new disc-to-digital feature that will allow users to get a digital copy of their physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X games. It's been speculated that this is to prepare players for a transition to a more digital-focused next-generation console.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Xbox Is Letting Players Digitize Their Physical Games, Starting Next Week for Select Users
items.description: Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library.

The new feature will roll out to Xbox Insiders starting on August 31 before making its way to everyone at an unknown future date. This new initiative leaked earlier this summer and will be a way to allow players to put their Xbox One and Xbox Series X discs into their console and get a fully usable digital version.

Your discs will also remain playable, but if you give the game to someone else and they insert that copy into their console, you will lose access to your digital license as well. It's not only great for the sake of convenience, but perhaps more notably, it also enables you to stream the game through the cloud or access it on other devices via Xbox Play Anywhere if the game supports those features.

That means you don't have to have the game installed at all, and you can play it on PC, the ROG Ally, or even your mobile devices. Unfortunately, Microsoft made no mention of this feature being supported with original Xbox or Xbox 360 games, so don't expect those right now. Additionally, not every game will be supported off the bat. However, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the company will support thousands of games when this feature launches, with more added over time. Will that eventually encompass Xbox 360 titles? It's hard to say.

"Your physical game library is more than a collection of discs," said Sharma. "It holds years of memories and stories worth preserving. Starting next week, Xbox Insiders can unlock a digital entitlement for supported physical games. We’ll start with thousands of titles and add more as we can."

Some have speculated that this move is happening to create a smooth transition between this generation and the next Xbox, which may be a digital-only device. Microsoft has yet to confirm such a thing, but given PlayStation won't support discs starting in 2028, physical gaming media may be less of a standard next-gen. Regardless, this is a great feature that will definitely offer a lot of benefits to those who enjoy physical media.
